title: ASSIMILATE EP, by FLX
description:
“FLX’s Assimilate traverses darker terrain, its acid-industrial mood kicks off with “Precinct” as the title track delves into early Aphex Twin blips and bleeps—simply put: hard-edged electronics with a moving pulse. Floating into downtempo streams, “Obxd Funk” is an aptly-titled track that flings broken beats with a groovy, slow-motion and head-bobbing rhythm. On “J-41,” FLX flexes his drill’n bass muscles, glitch’n clicks rattling from all directions, the scattered percussive overflow is balanced by distant background ambient shifting. With “Collision,” FLX migrates to more traditional forms—direct, in your face techno with an emotive and upbeat backdrop that smudges the lines between braindance and synth-wave. Closing with “Tracer,” here we find another downtempo behemoth—its mysterious tones and drones slice there way between abstract electronic beats and acidic warbles. Overall a fine-tuned extended player that cuts through minimal soundscapes while simultaneously shattering bass bins with highly energetic tracks.“

https://igloomag.com/reviews/flx-nike-vomita-double-review-evel

title: Rain Temple, by 2814
description:
“2814 are one of the most innovative musical acts in recent memory. Blending breathtaking ambient soundscapes and futuristic downtempo experiments with a gorgeous sense of electronic melancholy and urban atmosphere, the ever­-elusive duo’s sound is defined by their brilliant adoration for warped, hypnagogic nostalgia and the simultaneous outlook into a futuristic dystopian setting – a winning combination of loss and optimism translated through a heavily altered new age lens. Rain Temple, their third full­-length album, represents a new chapter in 2814′s sound: sprawling synth drones, beautifully distant vocals, swirling percussion, and an ethereal sonic aura tie together a simply masterful record. HKE and t e l e p a t h have once again created a stunning artistic statement that exceeds expectation and goes far beyond most modern ambient music, reminding us that beyond our late night somber and eternal wonder, we all remain.”

–words by Marcel Foley of  www.marcelsmusicjournal.com

title: Jettison Mind Hatch, by Tipper
description: “Jettison Mind Hatch is Tipper‘s thirteenth full-length album and it’s a gorgeous foray into the realms of sound which are crafted, despite not breaking new ground in any particular way. Clocking in at just a little over fifty minutes, it provides ample time for moods, feelings, and textures to develop and toy around with each other. It also gives the listener plenty of time to immerse himself into the journey. The immersive quality of the album is only catalyzed by the absolutely pristine production value that is present. The amount of tinkering with each and every little inflection really pays off. There is a resounding spatial quality that emerges from the sound stage of the songs, giving the listener a sensation that could be only compared to drifting in space or in an endless ocean. The crispness of every tone is also a big plus regarding this aspect, offering quite a detailed view, akin to watching the sun in 4K resolution on a projector” – Everything is noise

title: The Grid, by Mega Drive
description: This is a fairly new release, which came out sometime toward the end of 2017. When I first bought it, I thought it was OK–not quite the same drive, production, and overall style as 198XAD; which is what I was hoping for based on the title. It’s definitely a step in the same direction that Seas of Infinity took, which I thought was OK as well. The more I listen to this album now, I’ve grown more attached to it as a whole. While it is a bit more on the ambient side, it continues to capture the nostalgia of 80s synthwave, which I appreciate more. I would definitely recommend this to anyone into synthwave, and will probably go back and listen to Seas of Inifity again.

title: Invisible hands, by Subtrakt
description: Just shy of thirty minutes, this ep picks up where last year’s Inside Information left off. Three tracks of elegant, shimmering tones that seem to flow into each other very nicely. Compared to previous albums, these tracks have very minmal percussive elements that are accompanied by pianos but stil manages to find the right balance. The fourth tracks is an atmospheric remix of Across The Grain by Monolog which fits very nicely with the rest of the track to the point where you almost wouldn’t recoginize it being a remix.

summary: Miles to Midnight, by Atrium Carceri, Cities Last Broadcast, God Body Disconnect
title: Miles to Midnight, by Atrium Carceri, Cities Last Broadcast, God Body Disconnect
description: This album features a collaboration between three independent dark ambient arists. The music itself is exactly what you’d picture a gritty crime noir soundtrack to sound like. Complete with smokey atmospheres, subtle jazz percussion and horns, and the occasional tape loops. Highly recommended for anyone into dark ambient and film noir.

title: [AR_073] Microscopists - Ghost Payload / Abstrakt Reflections
excerpt: "Ghost Payload" is Microscopists first record, and explores the relationship between humans and their technology.
description: The latest release on Abstrakt Relfections brings us 9 epic tracks by Microscopists. The album begins with the sort of atmospheric clicks and cuts as one would expect from other releases, but later songs like “Morbid Calculus” ties in an intricate weave of post-rock style guitars and some minimal voices; think something off of early to mid Neurot Recordings but with the vocal style of, say, Katatonia. Needless to say, this is refreshing release and definitely worth the donation. Check it out.
